column1: # relative-time golden — the cross-language ladder pin (finding F5, Task 1.4).
# every row is one (now, then) pair in epoch milliseconds plus the label BOTH
# ladders must return for it. the `expected` column was derived BY HAND from the
# documented ladder — elapsed < 60 s -> "1m"; < 60 min -> "<n>m"; < 24 h ->
# "<n>h"; 1-6 whole calendar days -> "<n>d"; 7+ days -> "Mon D"; a different
# year appends ", YY" — never by running either implementation and pasting its
# output. that is the point: both sides are asserted against the same
# independent literals, so one ladder drifting shows up as a mismatch instead of
# two implementations agreeing with each other.
# asserted at LOCAL WALL-CLOCK. every instant is noon America/Chicago (UTC-6 on
# these dates, UTC-5 for the two October/March rows), i.e. as far as the table
# can be from midnight and from a DST transition, so no row's calendar-day
# bucket can be flipped by the host's zone. a host in another zone, or a table
# regenerated across a zone change, must recompute every row: this pin protects
# the ladder's shape, not its relationship to a particular offset.
# read by Tests/ArcAgentWebUITests/RelativeTimeParityTests.swift (Swift ladder,
# through AppState.relTimeLabel with `now` injected) and by
# Scripts/relative-time-parity.mjs (JS ladder, extracted from
# Sources/ArcWebUI/Assets/overlay.js and evaluated under a frozen clock).
